# datalogic-rs

> JSONLogic (json-logic) rules engine and sandboxed
> expression evaluator: one Rust core with official bindings for
> Node.js, browser/edge WASM, Python, Go, Java (JVM), .NET, and PHP,
> plus an embeddable React visual rule editor and step-through
> debugger. Business rules are plain JSON data: store them in a
> database, ship them over an API, change logic without a redeploy.
> Apache-2.0.

Key facts (current release 5.8.1): rules compile once to opcode
programs and evaluate in a reusable memory arena (10.3 ns geomean across
the 51-suite benchmark matrix); the core is `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`
with no eval, no I/O, and no scripting runtime, so user-submitted rules
cannot run host code; the same 2,128-case conformance battery (66 suites)
runs in CI against the core and through the bindings, so every language
gives the same result; 84 built-in operators including datetime,
string/array/object extensions, error handling (try/throw), tensor
marshalling, and flagd-compatible feature-flag operators (fractional,
sem_ver) with murmur3 bucketing byte-compatible with OpenFeature flagd.

Install per language: Rust `cargo add datalogic-rs` · Node.js
`npm i @goplasmatic/datalogic-node` · Browser/Edge WASM
`npm i @goplasmatic/datalogic-wasm` · Python `pip install datalogic-py`
(typed, PEP 561) · Go
`go get github.com/GoPlasmatic/datalogic-rs/bindings/go/v5` · JVM
`io.github.goplasmatic:datalogic` (JDK 22+) · .NET
`dotnet add package Goplasmatic.Datalogic` · PHP
`composer require goplasmatic/datalogic` (PHP 8.4+, ext-ffi) · React UI
`npm i @goplasmatic/datalogic-ui`. Cargo: `datalogic-rs = "5"`; Maven /
Gradle: `io.github.goplasmatic:datalogic:5.8.1`.

API shape (the same in every language): one-shot `apply(rule, data)`;
`Engine` → `compile(rule)` → `rule.evaluate(data)` for hot paths;
`Session` for arena-reuse loops; `DataHandle` for parse-once payloads;
typed results (bool/int/float) for predicates; batch evaluation;
custom operators registered as host-language callbacks; templating
per engine or per rule (`compileTemplate`); step-by-step trace output.
Rule analysis: `check(rule)` returns diagnostics (unknown operator with a
"did you mean" suggestion, wrong argument count) located by JSON Pointer;
`compileChecked(rule)` refuses a rule with errors (`CompileError`);
`rule.facts()` lists the data paths and operators a rule uses;
`engine.operators()` is the operator catalogue. Config
`"missing_var": "error"` makes a missing data path raise
`VariableNotFound` instead of reading `null`.

- [Introduction](https://goplasmatic.github.io/datalogic-rs/introduction.html):
  what the engine is and when to use it
- [Quick start](https://goplasmatic.github.io/datalogic-rs/getting-started/quick-start.html):
  first evaluation in every language
- [Operator reference](https://goplasmatic.github.io/datalogic-rs/operators/overview.html):
  all 84 built-in operators with examples
- [Language guides](https://goplasmatic.github.io/datalogic-rs/rust/overview.html):
  per-binding chapters (Rust, Node, WASM, Python, Go, JVM, .NET, PHP, React UI)
- [Configuration](https://goplasmatic.github.io/datalogic-rs/advanced/configuration.html):
  NaN, division, truthiness, missing-variable and operator-family settings
- [Security & sandboxing](https://goplasmatic.github.io/datalogic-rs/advanced/security.html):
  the sandbox guarantees and what remains the host's job
- [Migration guide](https://goplasmatic.github.io/datalogic-rs/migration.html):
  v4 to v5, and the behaviour changes in 5.8.0
- [How it compares](https://goplasmatic.github.io/datalogic-rs/comparison.html):
  vs json-logic-js, json-logic-engine, GoRules ZEN, CEL
- [Performance](https://goplasmatic.github.io/datalogic-rs/performance.html):
  benchmark methodology and numbers

## Try it

- [Live playground](https://goplasmatic.github.io/datalogic-rs/playground/):
  visual editor and step-through debugger running the real engine (WASM)
- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/GoPlasmatic/datalogic-rs):
  source, examples for every language under bindings/<lang>/examples/
- [Rust API docs](https://docs.rs/datalogic-rs): docs.rs reference

## Notes for code generation

- Rule and data inputs: Node and Python accept native objects; WASM,
  Go, JVM, .NET, and PHP take JSON strings at the primary surface.
- Compile once and reuse the compiled rule; compiled rules are
  thread-safe in every binding. Sessions are single-threaded.
- Errors carry a stable tag (`ParseError`, `InvalidOperator`,
  `InvalidArguments`, `VariableNotFound`, `TypeError`, `Thrown`, ...)
  with the same taxonomy in every language, plus the innermost failing
  operator. Arithmetic on non-numeric input surfaces as `Thrown` whose
  payload is `{"type": "NaN"}`; `NaN` itself is not a tag.
- An unknown operator compiles and fails only when evaluation reaches it;
  call `check` or `compileChecked` to catch it up front.
- `and` / `or` return the deciding operand, not a boolean, so the
  json-logic-js default-value idiom works unchanged:
  `{"or": [{"var": "nickname"}, "Anonymous"]}` yields the nickname when
  it is truthy and `"Anonymous"` otherwise.
- WASM: build an `Engine` (`new Engine(options)`) and use
  `engine.evalStr`, `engine.compile` and `rule.evaluate`. The free
  `evaluate` / `evaluateWithTrace` functions and the `CompiledRule` class
  are deprecated in 5.8.0 and removed in 6.0. In Node and WASM,
  `evaluateNumber` is deprecated; use `evaluateFloat` or `evaluateInt`.
- The old v4 npm package `@goplasmatic/datalogic` no longer exists on
  the registry; use `@goplasmatic/datalogic-node` (native Node) or
  `@goplasmatic/datalogic-wasm` (browser/edge).
